plan: In a single-round auction with complete rationality, the dominant strategy is the "truth-telling" equilibrium. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot game, I should bid close to my true value of $30, but slightly below to maximize potential profit. A strategic bid around $29.9 would allow me to win if others bid lower while protecting some potential profit margin.

In a single-round auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. Since my value is $7, I want to bid just low enough to potentially win but not overpay. A bid around $6-$6.5 balances the risk of losing with the risk of overpaying. This strategy assumes other bidders are also using similar rational reasoning, trying to bid strategically relative to their own private values.

In a single-round auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid close to, but not exactly at, my private value. Since the third-price auction incentivizes truthful bidding, I want to bid strategically to maximize potential profit. With a $36 value, I'll bid slightly below my true value to protect against overpaying, but high enough to likely win. A bid around $35 seems rational.
